title: Ashura: the fast of Musa
hook: the Prophet ﷺ fasted the tenth of Muharram in thanks for Musa's rescue (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the Hijri year, counted from the emigration to Medina. Your line was a new year from the hijra.

A newcomer has just arrived in a town, tired, after a dangerous journey. On one particular day, he notices that many of his new neighbors aren't eating. He asks why. They tell him: this is the day God rescued Musa and his people from Pharaoh and drowned Pharaoh's army, and Musa fasted on this day in thanks, so we fast too. According to Bukhari, that's roughly what happened when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Medina and saw the Jewish community fasting on the tenth day of the month.
screen: `A NEW TOWN, A DAY OF FASTING.`

segments.voice: The day is called 'Ashura, from 'ashara, ten. It's the tenth of Muharram. Bukhari records Ibn 'Abbas describing the scene. The Prophet asked about the fast, heard the reason, and said that Muslims too had a claim to Musa, a bond with him. So he fasted that day, and told his companions to fast it. Another report, from 'A'isha, says the Quraysh in Mecca had already fasted 'Ashura before Islam, and the Prophet had fasted it there. Then, once the fast of Ramadan was made a duty, 'Ashura became optional: whoever wished to fast it fasted, and whoever wished to leave it left it. A hadith in Muslim's collection says the fast of 'Ashura is hoped to wipe away the faults of the year before. And another, also in Muslim, says that late in his life the Prophet resolved that if he lived another year he would fast the ninth as well. He died before that year came, which is why some fast the ninth with the tenth, and some the tenth with the eleventh. So among Sunni Muslims, the tenth of Muharram is mostly a day of fasting in gratitude, rooted in an older story: the sea opening, the people crossing, the army gone. Tomorrow, the same date holds a very different memory, one that came later, and is kept with grief.
screen: `'ASHURA: THE TENTH.` · `WE HAVE A CLAIM TO MUSA TOO.` · `OPTIONAL ONCE RAMADAN CAME.` · `THE NINTH AND THE TENTH.`

segments.voice: Think of a time you were pulled out of something: an illness you recovered from, a mistake that turned out less badly than it could have, a person who showed up at the right moment. Stay with that memory for a moment. If you pray, you can give thanks for it, the way the fast of 'Ashura gives thanks for a rescue.
'Ashura. The tenth of Muharram, which the Prophet fasted in thanks for Musa's rescue from Pharaoh. Today's word.
Your line: thanks for a rescue. An old story, kept with gratitude. That's day five hundred three.

howItsDone: Many Sunni Muslims fast on the tenth of Muharram, often with the ninth or eleventh as well, as a voluntary fast of gratitude; the day is observed differently in Shia communities, as a day of mourning.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2004 (the fast in Medina, Ibn 'Abbas)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2002 (the Quraysh fasted 'Ashura; optional after Ramadan)

notes: No direct quotations; all hadith paraphrased. Numbers (Bukhari 2002, 2004; Muslim 1134, 1162) cited from memory; confirm.

The Prophet's words in Bukhari 2004 are often rendered 'we have more right to Musa than you'; the script softens this to 'Muslims too had a claim to Musa, a bond with him' to avoid a comparison. A Keeper should confirm the paraphrase is fair.
The 'tenth day of the month' in Medina: scholars discuss how the Jewish fast (Yom Kippur on 10 Tishri, or another fast) aligned with the lunar date; the script avoids naming the Jewish fast. Confirm.
Fasting the tenth and eleventh as an alternative is a scholarly recommendation; confirm.
